key_facts: Patient is an obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption the night prior
Visual acuity is no light perception in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye
Intraocular pressure is 37 mm Hg in the right eye and 21 mm Hg in the left eye
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

raw.rationale: The patient's sudden vision loss in one eye, along with findings of delayed retinal arterial filling, patchy hyperfluorescence, and poor vascular perfusion on fluorescein angiography, and severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on optical coherence tomography, are highly suggestive of central retinal artery occlusion.

rejected.label: Glaucoma
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated intraocular pressure, the presence of severe retinal disorganization, delayed choroidal filling, and poor vascular perfusion points more towards an acute vascular event like central retinal artery occlusion rather than glaucoma alone.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
rejected.why: There is no mention of systemic symptoms such as headache, jaw claudication, or polymyalgia rheumatica, which are commonly associated with giant cell arteritis, and the patient's age and presentation do not strongly suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Optic Neuritis
rejected.why: Optic neuritis typically presents with pain on eye movement and a decrease in visual acuity, but the extensive retinal and vascular findings in this case, including delayed choroidal filling and severe retinal disorganization, are not characteristic of optic neuritis.

rejected.label: Relative Afferent Pupillary Defect
rejected.why: A relative afferent pupillary defect is a sign that can be associated with various conditions affecting the retina or optic nerve, but it is not a diagnosis in itself and does not explain the full spectrum of the patient's presentation.
